note: The OLG covers the core SE income averaging rules well: annualization over 12 months for annual income earned in a shorter period (Self-Employment SNAP > Averaging Self-Employment Income), prorating for income covering only part of the year (Anticipating Self-Employment Income), and the anticipated income calculation method with capital gains. The OLG also addresses fluctuating income averaging generally (Types of Earned Income > Income Averaging: 'if the income fluctuates, the household may elect to average the income over the certification period'). However, several FNS requirements lack explicit OLG coverage: (1) the 'steady SE income' exception — FNS explicitly states no averaging/annualizing/prorating is needed for steady SE income that can be anticipated month-to-month, while the OLG only implies this through its 'Anticipating Self-Employment Income' section for non-averaged SE income; (2) no guidance on handling unreported SE income sources discovered post-certification; (3) no procedures for correcting SE income when the household reported incorrectly, policy was misapplied, or a computation error occurred. Items 2 and 3 are framed as QC reviewer tasks in FNS but have caseworker relevance when errors are discovered during case maintenance. SE income verification is addressed in the Types of Earned Income page (business records, tax returns, documents showing gross income and expenses) but not on the SE-specific OLG page itself.
